title: Introduction to the Profession
description: Introduces science and engineering as professions: how problems are solved and how solutions are judged against computational, financial, and social limits.

title: Introduction to Computer Programming for Engineers
description: High-level programming as an engineering problem-solving tool, with basic data structures, algorithms, and documentation. For students new to coding.

title: Introduction to Computer Programming
description: Programming for problem solving for students with little or no coding background, covering data structures, algorithms, and documentation.

title: Computing Principles
description: Core computing ideas: abstraction, algorithms, data, programming, the internet, and the global effects of computing.

title: Object-Oriented Programming I
description: Object-oriented programming as a problem-solving tool, with basic data structures, algorithms, and documentation. Made for students with little or no programming experience.

title: Object-Oriented Programming II
description: Advanced object-oriented topics such as dynamic data structures, recursion, searching, and sorting. For students in CS and CS-related programs.
prerequisites: CS 115 with min. grade of C

title: Artificial Intelligence Foundations
description: A hands-on introduction to AI for all majors: practical tool use, ethics, privacy, and human-AI collaboration.

title: Accelerated Introduction to Computer Science
description: Problem solving and design with an object-oriented language. Introduces problem-solving techniques, algorithms, and data structures.
prerequisites: CS 104 with min. grade of C or CS 105 with min. grade of C or CS 110 with min. grade of C or CS 115 with min. grade of C or Graduate standing

title: Discrete Structures
description: Formal mathematical structures for problems and computation: Boolean algebra, first-order logic, recursive structures, graphs, and abstract language models.

title: Data Structures and Algorithms
description: Implementing and using essential data structures, and analyzing basic sorting and searching algorithms and how they relate to those structures.

title: Programming Paradigms and Patterns
description: Programming patterns through a functional lens using Haskell: monads, concurrency, domain-specific languages, and property-based testing.

title: Computer Organization and Assembly Language Programming
description: Internal computer architecture and how hardware, instruction sets, and high-level languages relate, with assembly language exercises.
prerequisites: CS 116* or CS 201*, An asterisk (*) designates a course which may be taken concurrently.

title: Systems Programming
description: Parts of multilayer software systems such as device drivers, systems software, and user interfaces, and the design of interrupt-driven and event-driven software.

title: Special Projects
description: Special projects. Needs instructor permission.

title: Introduction to Advanced Studies I
description: Prepares students for graduate study with data structures and algorithms in Java and their math foundations. Does not count toward M.S. or Ph.D. credit.

title: Introduction to Advanced Studies II
description: Layered construction of software systems, from device drivers to user interfaces, and how architecture shapes software.
prerequisites: CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S

title: Foundations to Advanced Studies
description: Combines CS 401 and CS 402 into one course: data structures, software development, architecture, assembly language, event handling, and multithreading.

title: Introduction to Discrete Structures and Algorithms
description: Basic discrete math and algorithm design, with proofs, worst-case and average-case analysis, and approximation and randomized algorithms.

title: Computer Graphics
description: Display devices, 2D and 3D vector graphics, image generation, transformations, hidden-line removal, and projections.
prerequisites: (CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S) and (MATH 332 or MATH 333)

title: Introduction to Human-Computer Interaction
description: Human-computer interaction through the design process and a semester project: prototyping, user testing, ethics, and accessibility.

title: Data Mining
description: Data mining methods such as market basket analysis, nearest neighbor, decision trees, and clustering, practiced through implementation.
prerequisites: CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S or CS 403

title: Database Organization
description: Database architectures (relational, hierarchical, network, object) and database interfaces such as SQL.
prerequisites: CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S or CS 403

title: Information Retrieval
description: Information retrieval theory and search engine parts. Students build a prototype search engine.
prerequisites: CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S

title: Introduction to Algorithms
description: Design, behavior, and analysis of algorithms, with focus on searching, sorting, and combinatorial algorithms, and worst-case, amortized, and expected bounds.
prerequisites: (CS 331 and CS 330) or (CS 331 and MATH 230) or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S or CS 403

title: Programming Languages and Translators
description: Common programming languages with precise definitions and practical use, plus an introduction to scanning, parsing, and compiler design.
prerequisites: (CS 331 and CS 330) or (CS 331 and MATH 230) or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S or CS 403

title: Compiler Construction
description: Students build a compiler step by step: syntax trees, intermediate representations, type checking, and function implementation.

title: Object Oriented Design and Programming
description: Methods for object-oriented design and programming, and how the object model is built in different languages.
prerequisites: CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S or CS 403

title: Operating Systems
description: Operating system concepts, including scheduling, process management, deadlocks, and memory management.
prerequisites: CS 351 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 and CS 402 or CSSP 402 or CS 403

title: Introduction to Parallel and Distributed Computing
description: Parallel and distributed computing across cloud, grid, cluster, supercomputer, and many-core systems.

title: Data Communications
description: Data communication protocols and interfaces, focused on the lower four layers of the ISO-OSI model.

title: Introduction to Wireless Networks and Performance
description: A survey of wireless networks of all ranges, including satellite, with their performance and challenges.
prerequisites: CS 350 or ECE 242 CS 401 or CSSP 401 and CS 402 or CSSP 402 or CS 403

title: Introduction to Information Security
description: Computer and information security: defenses against malicious software, encryption, and OS, database, and network security.

title: Computer Architecture
description: The functional parts of digital computers at the register transfer level: arithmetic, memory, I/O, and instruction processing.

title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
description: Methods for controlling autonomous agents: heuristic search, knowledge representation, and probabilistic reasoning.
prerequisites: (CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S) and (MATH 474* or MATH 475*), An asterisk (*) designates a course which may be taken concurrently.

title: Artificial Intelligence Language Understanding
description: Theory and methods that let systems understand human language and pull information out of text.
prerequisites: (CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S) and (MATH 474* or MATH 475*), An asterisk (*) designates a course which may be taken concurrently.

title: Information and Knowledge Management Systems
description: How organizations capture, share, and apply knowledge, plus trends like cloud, AI, and crisis knowledge management.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Machine learning ideas and algorithms: classification, clustering, and regression, including k-means, decision trees, naive Bayes, and neural networks.
prerequisites: MATH 151 or MATH 192 or STAT 225 or BUS 221 or PSYC 203 and CS 116 or CS 201 or CS 401 or ITM 311

title: Computers and Society
description: How computer technology affects society, past and present, and the social issues it raises.
prerequisites: COM 421 or COM 424 or COM 425 or COM 428 or COM 435

title: Software Engineering I
description: Software engineering principles and practice: quality, process models, requirements, design, testing, and maintenance, with a team project.
prerequisites: (CS 331 or CS 401 or CSSP 401 with min. grade of S or CS 403) and CS 425

title: Undergraduate Research
description: Undergraduate research. Needs instructor permission.

title: Introduction to Computer Science Research
description: Prepares undergraduate computer science majors to do research.

title: Topics in Computer Science
description: A current computer science topic that changes from semester to semester.

title: Special Projects
description: Special projects.

title: Calculus I

prerequisites: Raw Math score of 80 or MATH 145 with min. grade of C or MATH 148 with min. grade of C

title: Calculus II
description: Transcendental functions, integration methods, improper integrals, polar coordinates, and series.
prerequisites: MATH 149 with min. grade of C or MATH 151 with min. grade of C

title: Introduction to Discrete Math
description: Sets, logic, relations, functions, induction, and basic counting.

title: Multivariate and Vector Calculus
description: Calculus in three dimensions: partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector analysis.

title: Introduction to Differential Equations
description: First- and higher-order linear differential equations, Laplace transforms, and systems.

title: Linear Algebra: Theory and Applications

prerequisites: MATH 251*, An asterisk (*) designates a course which may be taken concurrently.

title: Matrix Algebra and Complex Variables
description: Matrix operations, eigenvalues, and linear systems, plus complex analysis such as contour integrals and residues.

title: Probability and Statistics
description: Probability distributions, estimation, hypothesis tests, confidence intervals, and linear regression.

title: Probability
description: Probability theory, random variables, joint distributions, limit theorems, and simulation.

title: Computer Vision
description: Core computer vision topics and how deep neural networks are applied to them.

title: Advanced Data Mining
description: Advanced algorithms, such as support vector machines, through a large project.
prerequisites: CS 422 with min. grade of C

title: Deep Learning
description: The math, algorithms, and GPU tools behind deep neural networks, with uses in vision, audio, and language.

title: Reinforcement Learning
description: Learning decision-making policies through interaction: bandits, Markov decision processes, and core learning methods.
prerequisites: CS 480 with min. grade of C or MATH 474 with min. grade of C or MATH 475

title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence
description: Advanced AI topics, from search and probabilistic reasoning to deep learning, reinforcement learning, and AI ethics.
prerequisites: CS 480 with min. grade of C

title: Probabilistic Graphical Models
description: Models for reasoning under uncertainty: representation, learning, and inference across several fields.

title: Machine Learning
description: Core machine learning ideas, algorithms, and evaluation, including regression, kernel methods, and neural networks.
prerequisites: CS 430 with min. grade of C

title: Natural Language Processing
description: Computational methods for human language, including parsing, text generation, and discourse.
prerequisites: CS 430 with min. grade of C

title: Statistical Learning
description: Modern methods for learning from data: regression, classification, kernel methods, and support vector machines.
prerequisites: (MATH 474 with min. grade of C or MATH 475 with min. grade of C or Graduate standing) and (MATH 350 with min. grade of C or Graduate standing)

title: Bayesian Computational Statistics
description: Bayesian inference theory and data analysis: priors, posteriors, estimation, testing, and computational methods in statistical software.

prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: Industrial Culture
description: How modern industrial society developed, and how science and technology shaped culture, using history, literature, and philosophy.
prerequisites: IIT Communication Placement score of 102, COM 111, COM 101, or qualifying ACT, SAT, or writing test scores

description: How engineering, design, and technology relate to ethics, public media, and writing. Covers reading data-driven texts, basic data visualization, and arguing from data to professional and public audiences.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

description: Introduces the humanities by tracing cultural change linked to Darwin's theory of evolution, with readings from literature, philosophy, and science.
prerequisites: COM 101, COM 111, IIT Communication Placement score of 102, or qualifying ACT, SAT, or writing test scores

title: Life Stories
description: Interdisciplinary study of mostly American autobiographies as a genre, and of the historical and philosophical forces behind the writers' lives. Syllabi vary and may feature figures such as Franklin, Angelou, and Malcolm X.
prerequisites: COM 101, COM 111, IIT Communication Placement score of 102, or qualifying ACT, SAT, or writing test scores

title: Digital Culture
description: Major topics in digital culture, including the technical and cultural history of the internet, with academic writing and humanities research methods.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: Topics in Humanities
description: First-time or one-time offerings of topics equal to HUM 202, 204, 206, and 208. Introduces the humanities at IIT with intensive writing instruction.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

description: Extends the study of industrial society and its cultural effects from the late eighteenth century to today, using interdisciplinary readings. Writing-intensive.

title: Age of Darwin

prerequisites: COM 101, COM 111, or IIT Communication Placement score of 102

title: Life Stories
description: Interdisciplinary study of biographies and autobiographies as a genre, and of the historical and philosophical contexts of their subjects' lives. Writing-intensive.
prerequisites: COM 101, COM 111, or IIT Communication Placement score of 102

title: Seminar in Humanities
description: A current or long-standing humanities topic that does not fit standard categories.

title: Independent Reading/Research
description: Independent reading or research under faculty direction.

title: Foundational Research Methods
description: Research methods and current scholarship for advanced humanities students. Students run self-designed research projects and aim to write a draft article for a humanities journal.

title: World Civilizations to 1500
description: Major civilizations from prehistory to 1500 across Eurasia, Africa, and the Americas: river civilizations, trade, states and empires, and major religions.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: World Civilizations Since 1500
description: The making of the modern world through global geopolitical, social, and economic ties, from colonization and the Columbian Exchange to world wars, decolonization, and the 21st century.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: Western Civilization to 1500
description: Western history to 1500, from early states in Mesopotamia, Greece, and Rome through medieval Europe, the Crusades, the Black Death, and the Renaissance.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: Western Civilization Since 1500
description: Western history from 1500: the Reformation, the Scientific Revolution, the Enlightenment, revolutions, nationalism, imperialism, the world wars, the Cold War, and decolonization.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: History of the United States to 1877
description: U.S. history to 1877: colonization, the Revolution, the Constitution, the early republic, slavery, the Civil War, and Reconstruction.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: History of the United States Since 1877
description: How the U.S. gained economic and military power and used it at home and abroad, from the Gilded Age through the world wars, Civil Rights, and the early 2000s.

title: History of Chicago
description: Urban institutions in historical context, with Chicago as a case study: political machines, reform movements, planning agencies, ethnic neighborhoods, and organized crime.

description: The people, places, institutions, politics, and culture of Chicago during federal Prohibition, and the factors that shaped the city's experience.

title: Chicago LGBTQ History
description: How LGBTQ narratives, cultures, and organizations developed in Chicago, within local, national, and international history.

title: A History of Artificial Intelligence from Turing to the Present
description: AI from the mid-20th century to today: technical developments, the philosophy behind AI, and its cultural, economic, and environmental effects.

title: History of Video Games
description: The technical and cultural history of video games, with scholarly writing and humanities research methods.

title: Topics in History

title: Seminar in History
description: A topic of current or lasting historical interest, announced by the instructor when scheduled.

title: Independent Reading and Research
description: Independent reading and research for advanced students. Needs department consent.

title: Judgment and Decision-Making
description: Good reasoning, the psychology and philosophy of judgment errors and biases, their effects on people and societies, and ways to improve judgment.

title: Rationality and Science Policy
description: Evidence-based look at science policy problems such as group polarization, conspiracy theories, and deference to experts, and the reasoning skills citizens and officials need.

title: Philosophy and Psychology of Language
description: Evidence on the nature and origins of language from philosophical and psychological angles: animal communication, reference, meaning, and the biology of language.

title: Influential Thinkers
description: In-depth study of one outstanding philosopher, chosen by the instructor.

title: Introduction to Philosophy
description: Philosophical questions about the mind and its assumptions across philosophy, psychology, neuroscience, and AI, and the relation between minds, bodies, and machines.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: Philosophy of Medicine
description: Health, disease, and illness, and related philosophical and policy issues: clinical trial evidence, bias in care, AI in medicine, disability, and mental illness.

title: Ethics
description: Fundamental issues in moral philosophy.

title: Ethics of Technology and Communication
description: Ethical questions about technology and communication: algorithmic bias, privacy and surveillance, consent and manipulation, and digital environmental impact, using case studies.

title: Topics in Philosophy
description: A current philosophical topic announced by the instructor when scheduled.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Philosophy and Ethics
description: Ethical arguments and principles in AI and robotics: algorithmic bias, machine sentience, self-driving car decision rules, and the moral and legal status of robots.

title: Bioethics
description: Ethical and social issues in life sciences and biomedicine, such as gene editing, stem cells, neurotechnology, human enhancement, and climate change, with an introduction to ethical theory.

title: Trustworthy AI
description: Ethical aspects of AI, focused on trustworthy AI principles such as autonomy, harm prevention, fairness, explainability, privacy, and accountability, judged through use cases.

title: Philosophy of Data Science
description: Philosophical questions about data, such as what data is and how it works as evidence, plus ethical issues like privacy, algorithmic bias, and computing's environmental impact.

title: Political Philosophy of Artificial Intelligence
description: Applies social contract theories to AI: algorithmic nudging and bias, expertise and chatbots, online platform politics, and digital surveillance.
prerequisites: HUM 100, 102, 104, 106, 108, or 180, or any HUM 200-299 course (may be taken concurrently)

title: Philosophy of Mind
description: The concept of mind as distinct from body, and what it means for psychology, AI, and neuroscience.

title: Seminar in Philosophy
description: A current philosophical topic announced by the instructor when scheduled.

title: Independent Study
description: Supervised individual research for advanced students. Needs instructor permission.

title: Graphic Novel
description: How comics moved beyond superhero stories after the 1970s to take on philosophical themes. Works by major and outside creators, plus comics theory. Not for credit to students who took LIT 380 Graphic Novel.

title: Influential Authors
description: The work of one influential author, chosen by the instructor. Examples include Tolkien, Garcia Marquez, and N. K. Jemisin.

title: Topics in Literature
description: A current or lasting literary topic set by the instructor. Examples include fantasy history, Victorian literature, and Realism.

title: Seminar in Literature
description: A literary topic of current or lasting interest, announced by the instructor when scheduled.

title: Workshop in Creative Writing
description: Writing fiction, poetry, or drama from a writer's view. Analyzes modern works and workshops student manuscripts.

title: Independent Reading and Research
description: Advanced independent study. Needs department consent.

prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: History of World Architecture II
description: Architecture worldwide from the Renaissance to the present, focused on specific cultures and architects alongside broader theories and strategies.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

description: Skills for describing, analyzing, and arguing about painting, sculpture, printmaking, and architecture. Covers art-historical methods, race and identity in interpretation, and how art is exhibited, using Chicago-area institutions.
prerequisites: Satisfaction of IIT's Basic Writing Proficiency Requirement

title: Topics in Art and Architecture History
description: A current or long-standing topic in art or architectural history, announced by the instructor when scheduled.

title: Independent Reading and Research
description: Independent reading and research for advanced students. Needs instructor permission.

title: Introduction to the Profession
description: Overview of psychology concepts, academic career planning, information literacy, communication, and professional skills.

title: Introduction to Recovery Support
description: Foundations of recovery philosophy, empowerment, listening skills, service planning, advocacy, and mentorship.

title: Ethical and Professional Issues in Recovery Support
description: Historical, philosophical, ethical, and legal issues in recovery support, with ethical decision-making and multicultural competence.

title: Evidence-Based Practices in Recovery Support
description: Evidence-based practices in mental health and substance use treatment, such as motivational interviewing and supported employment.

title: Special Topics and Populations in Recovery Support
description: Running peer groups and meeting the needs of special populations and topics like spirituality, sexuality, and telehealth.

title: Recovery Support Internship
description: Supervised community internship of at least 300 clock hours, with weekly individual and group supervision.

title: Introduction to Leadership: Concepts and Practices
description: Historical and current leadership theories, applied to practical leadership experiences.

description: Statistics for behavioral science: descriptive statistics, ANOVA, regression, correlation, and meta-analysis.

title: Research Methods in Behavioral Science
description: Experimental, survey, and field methods: ethics, research design, data collection and analysis, and report writing.

title: Social Psychology
description: How social conditions shape behavior and experience: social issues, human relations, prejudice, and leadership.

title: Industrial Psychology
description: Practical psychology applied to business and industry: work attitudes, selection, morale, safety, turnover, and training.

title: Introduction to Psychopathology
description: Cognitive, emotional, and behavioral disorders, with focus on diagnosis, causes, treatment, and research views.

title: Professional Skills
description: Applied skills in oral communication, conflict management, and interpersonal dynamics at work.

title: Human Motivation and Emotion
description: Major historical and current motivation theories, and their use in health care, sports, management, education, and gaming.

title: Applied Correlation and Regression
description: Applying correlation and regression to research on human behavior, with practical issues, analysis, and reporting of results.

title: Health Psychology
description: Psychological principles in health promotion, illness prevention, and treatment, including stress, coping, and specific diseases.

title: Human Sexuality
description: Sexual health and diversity: sexual response, gender identity, LGBT health, reproductive rights, and sexual communication.

title: Prejudice and Stigma
description: A social psychology view of how identities are stigmatized, the costs of prejudice, and research on reducing it.

title: Personality Theory
description: Overview of the main approaches to personality psychology.

title: Cross-Cultural Psychology
description: Cultural influences on psychological phenomena, including cross-cultural communication, workplace diversity, and national traits.

title: Clinical Psychology: Assessment and Treatment
description: Psychological testing, psychotherapy, and the work and trends of clinical psychologists.

title: Introduction to Sports Psychology
description: Psychological theories of sport and exercise: motivation, coaching, team dynamics, and performance strategies.

title: Health and Safety at Work
description: Occupational health psychology: how work organization affects employee health, stress, and well-being.

title: Topics in Psychology
description: A current psychology topic, announced by the instructor when scheduled.

title: Topics in Psychology
description: A current psychology topic, announced by the instructor when scheduled.
prerequisites: PSYC 221 or PSYC 301 or PSYC 303 or PSYC 310

description: Test development, testing techniques, and test use in education, organizations, and clinics, including scale construction.
prerequisites: PSYC 203 or PSYC 221 or PSYC 301, or Graduate standing

description: Historical, ethical, and legal foundations of rehabilitation and mental health counseling, including professional roles and service delivery.

description: Diversity issues in counseling, including culture, disability, gender, aging, and social justice, plus the psychosocial effects of disability.

description: Theories of learning: functionalist, associationist, cognitive, social, and neurophysiological views.

description: A systems view of organizational training: needs assessment, program design, transfer, and evaluation.
prerequisites: PSYC 221 or PSYC 301, or Graduate standing

title: Child and Adolescent Disorders
description: Major disorders of infancy, childhood, and adolescence, using a developmental psychopathology approach.

title: Behavior Design & User Testing
description: Applying behavioral science to technology design, with early consumer testing and lean testing methods.

title: Behavior Change Principles and Practice
description: Theories and techniques for behavior change, including stages of change, motivational interviewing, and contingency management.

title: Groups and Leadership at Work
description: A systems model of groups, group development stages, and leadership approaches, with activities on team member and leader roles.

title: Undergraduate Research Seminar I
description: Applied psychology research: review of current issues and work in faculty research programs.

title: Undergraduate Research Seminar II
description: Continues applied psychology research: review of current issues and work in faculty research programs.
prerequisites: (PSYC 221, PSYC 222, and PSYC 204), or Graduate standing

title: Senior Capstone Project I
description: Independent capstone project, which may include research, a literature review, data analysis, or an internship, guided by an advisor.

title: Senior Capstone Project II

description: Synthesis of issues and areas in psychology.

title: Integrative Psychology Seminar II
description: Brings together key and current research and ideas on major issues in psychology.

title: Undergraduate Psychology Seminar
description: Reports and discussion of current problems and issues in psychology.

title: Advanced Research
description: Advanced research for BSMP students.

description: How federal, state, regional, and local governments relate: federalism theory, constitutional basis, courts, administration, and current debates.

title: International Relations
description: Major theories for understanding global issues such as war, peace, security, human rights, political economy, development, and international organizations.

title: Democracy, Dictatorship, and Development
description: Comparative political analysis, applied to instability, conflict, and transitions to stable democracy.

title: Politics of Science and Technology
description: Links among science, technology, and politics, including scientific advice to government and the social effects of technological change.

title: Energy Policy

title: Public Administration
description: Administrative organization, decision-making, and structures, and the roles of government executives, fiscal procedures, and personnel management.

title: Urban Policy
description: Urban challenges such as economic change, fiscal strain, and marginalized groups, and how politicians and citizens respond. Also listed as SOC 354.

title: Global Political Economy
description: Economic, political, and cultural sides of globalization and international development.

title: Government and Politics in Africa
description: Current African politics in historical, economic, and cultural context, using country cases and regional issues.

title: East Asian Political Economy
description: Current East Asian politics in historical, economic, and cultural context, using country cases and regional issues.

title: Topics in Political Science
description: A current political science topic set by the instructor when scheduled.

title: International Law and Organizations
description: Global governance through political science and legal lenses, comparing frameworks such as those of the U.S., ICC, WTO, EU, and NAFTA.

title: Directed Readings in Political Science
description: Independent reading and analysis on specific problems, supervised by a political science faculty member. Up to 3 credits.

title: Microeconomics
